C141.title: LLMs answer "Who is X's parent?" but not the reverse
C141.paper_value_note: gpt-3.5-turbo(-0613) on the 1,513 released Exp. 2 rows, authors' scorer: P(forward correct | reverse correct) 0.663 − P(reverse correct | forward correct) 0.227 = 0.4365 [0.391, 0.482] (joint per pair = f·r, the one-sample-per-direction estimator)
C141.repro_source: experiments/run_minimal_setups/runs/added-b/runs/C141-chat_both-L200-gpt35-0125 (200 pairs x 10 samples), rescored with robust_parse (the panel's scorer: authors' prefix rule first, sentence-form fallback), same estimator. The authors' scorer alone gives 0.439 [0.333, 0.542].
C141.paper_date_note: arXiv v1 first submitted/posted 2023-09-21; later revisions do not reset release.
C141.citation: Berglund, L., Tong, M., Kaufmann, M., Balesni, M., Cooper Stickland, A., Korbak, T. & Evans, O. (2023). The Reversal Curse: LLMs trained on "A is B" fail to learn "B is A". ICLR 2024. arXiv:2309.12288
C141.note: Experiment 2 only (celebrity parents). Metric is the conditional asymmetry rather than the absolute forward − reverse gap (C141-gap, not counted), which does not shrink when a model simply knows fewer parents. panel run: variant robust, 600 pairs x 1 sample per direction; reliable needs the module headline reliable and >= 20 reverse-correct pairs. One scorer for all our runs: the panel runs and the paper-model reproduction both use the robust scorer (authors' rule first). The paper anchor is the authors' scorer on the released per-pair rates, which cannot be rescored because the raw outputs are unreleased; on the gpt-3.5-0125 rerun the robust scorer adds +0.037 to A (0.439 -> 0.476). Lenient name matching is a sensitivity.
